newsitem.title: FRANCE: France, ignoring U.N., continues Congo pullout.
newsitem.headline: France, ignoring U.N., continues Congo pullout.

text.p: France confirmed on Thursday that its pullout of 1,200 troops from Congo's capital Brazzaville, devastated by fighting, was expected to be completed before Sunday despite pleas from a U.N. envoy for some to stay.
"If the entire operation goes as planned, (it) should be completed before Sunday, June 22," the Defence Ministry said in a statement.

France started pulling out its force on Monday after evacuating more than 5,000 foreign nationals caught by the bloody political and ethnic dispute that has left the streets of the capital strewn with bodies.

It said the pullout was going as planned with the return of about 300 foreign legion troops to base in Chad on Wednesday . France is pulling out 1,200 troops, 350 tonnes of equipment and about 50 vehicles including light tanks and armoured personnel carriers.
Brazzaville enjoyed a second morning of calm on Thursday as a 72-hour ceasefire due to expire at midnight on Friday held firm.
U.N. envoy Mohamed Sahnoun on Wednesday urged France not to proceed with the pullout until a proposed African or international intervention force could replace them.

"The problem is going to be when the peace force can be deployed. I'm much more afraid of the vacuum that could exist in the short term," he told reporters in Brazzaville before flying to brief peace mediators in next-door Gabon.
The French ministry statement did not refer to Sahnouns' appeal.
Sahnoun met both warring leaders on Wednesday and said they had agreed to extend the truce as long as they could after the original deal expires.

The forces of President Pascal Lissouba and foes backing his predecessor Denis Sassou Nguesso are maintaining the ceasefire. Fighting broke out on June 5 when Lissouba's rump government forces tried to disarm Sassou Nguesso's "Cobras".
French General Rene Landrin said on Wednesday that around half of his men had already left and the rest would leave as planned by Sunday at the latest.
